children.text: Transforming a Content Website Into a High-Performance Shopify Store
For Parfums de Marly, moving to Shopify was not simply a platform migration. It was part of a broader website optimization project that combined
ecommerce development, redesign, SEO migration, and performance optimization

The existing website was primarily focused on presenting content and product information rather than supporting a complete online purchasing journey. The project therefore required us to preserve the site's existing content and SEO value while introducing a full ecommerce structure.
At the same time, the new website needed a more modern interface, stronger internal connections between content and products, and better technical performance.
From the beginning, the project centered on:
migrating the existing
WordPress website to Shopify
transforming the content-driven site into a complete ecommerce storefront;
preserving important SEO pages and existing content;
creating a new Shopify design and page structure;
improving internal linking between content and commercial pages;
optimizing
Shopify theme performance
and Core Web Vitals;
validating the complete website after migration.
Migrating Existing Content to Shopify
One of the first challenges was moving the existing content without losing the structure and SEO value that had already been established.
We migrated the site's core:
pages;
articles;
informational materials;
images;
other required media assets.
The content was then adapted to the new Shopify structure rather than simply copied into a different CMS.
This required balancing two objectives: maintaining important existing content while restructuring the website around its new ecommerce functionality.
Important SEO pages and valuable content were retained as part of the migration, providing continuity between the original website and the new Shopify implementation.
This approach made the migration more than a basic
WordPress to Shopify content transfer
. It became a structured
Shopify website migration
designed around both content preservation and the new commercial architecture.
Building a Complete Ecommerce Structure
The biggest functional change was the transformation of the website from a primarily content-focused platform into a complete online store.
The new ecommerce structure allows users to move through the entire purchasing journey directly on the website:
product discovery → product selection → add to cart → checkout
We implemented:
a structured product catalog;
product browsing and selection;
product information presentation;
add-to-cart functionality;
shopping cart functionality;
the complete purchasing flow;
order checkout through
Shopify Checkout
This created a new direct sales channel while allowing the site's existing informational content to remain an important part of the customer journey.
Instead of separating content and commerce, we connected them so that users could move naturally from learning about the products to purchasing them.
Connecting Content With Commerce
One of the key UX goals was to make the existing content more commercially useful without turning the website into a purely transactional storefront.
The new structure creates stronger relationships between informational pages and the product catalog.
This means content can support product discovery, while product pages provide a direct path toward purchase.
The resulting journey is more cohesive:
users discover relevant information;
they can explore the associated products;
product pages provide a clear next step;
products can be added directly to the cart;
the purchase can be completed through Shopify Checkout.
This created a stronger
content-to-commerce UX
and made the existing content a more integrated part of the ecommerce experience.
Redesigning the Shopify Storefront
The migration also included a complete redesign of the website's visual structure.
Rather than reproducing the original interface, we created a new design adapted specifically to the requirements of a Shopify ecommerce environment.
The redesign included:
a new visual structure;
redesigned key pages;
updated content block layouts;
a more consistent interface;
mobile-oriented interface improvements;
layouts designed to work across both content and commercial pages.
The main challenge was creating a unified visual system that could accommodate two different types of content: informational pages and ecommerce pages.
The result was a more coherent
Shopify custom storefront
where content, products, navigation, and purchasing functionality follow the same overall design language.
Custom Shopify Development for Content and Ecommerce
The new design was implemented directly in Shopify and adapted to the platform's ecommerce capabilities.
The development work focused on creating a structure that could support both existing content and new commercial functionality.
This included:
custom Shopify page structures;
ecommerce-oriented layouts;
reusable content elements;
product-focused components;
responsive interface behavior;
integration between content pages and the shopping experience.
This approach created a more flexible
Shopify custom development
foundation instead of treating the redesign as a collection of isolated page templates.
The result is a storefront architecture capable of supporting both editorial content and product-driven journeys within the same ecommerce system.
SEO Migration Built Around Existing Search Value

SEO was one of the most important parts of the migration because changing platforms and restructuring a website can create significant search visibility risks if the transition is not carefully controlled.
Before the migration, we analyzed the existing site structure and identified important pages and content that needed to be preserved.
The SEO work included:
analyzing the existing website structure;
preserving important SEO pages;
retaining valuable existing content;
configuring
URL redirects
where the structure changed;
optimizing
Title and Meta Description
elements for key pages;
reviewing heading structure;
improving internal linking;
checking technical indexing after migration.
Particular attention was given to the relationship between informational and commercial pages.
By improving internal linking between these areas, we created a stronger
Shopify internal linking structure
and clearer paths for both users and search engines.
The result was a migration strategy designed to preserve existing SEO value while providing a stronger technical foundation for the new ecommerce website.
Optimizing Titles, Meta Descriptions, and Heading Structure
The migration also provided an opportunity to improve important on-page SEO elements.
For key pages, we reviewed and optimized:
Title tags
Meta Descriptions
heading hierarchy;
page structure;
internal links.
These elements were considered alongside the new Shopify page architecture rather than optimized independently.
The goal was to create pages that were easier for users to understand while also providing a cleaner information hierarchy for search engines.
This formed part of a broader
Shopify SEO optimization
process rather than a one-time metadata update.
Shopify Performance Optimization
Performance was another major focus of the project.
The migration was used as an opportunity to review the technical resources loaded by the storefront and reduce unnecessary performance overhead.
Our optimization work included:
improving page loading behavior;
reducing unnecessary resources;
optimizing images;
optimizing third-party script loading;
reviewing the Shopify theme;
checking key performance indicators;
validating
Core Web Vitals

Performance optimization is particularly important for an ecommerce website because the user experience depends on multiple layers loading efficiently — from content and images to product interfaces, cart functionality, and third-party services.
By addressing these areas as part of the migration, we created a cleaner technical foundation for the new Shopify storefront.
Optimizing the Shopify Theme and Third-Party Resources
A significant part of the performance work focused on the relationship between the Shopify theme and the resources loaded by the website.
We reviewed unnecessary resources and worked on improving how assets, images, and third-party scripts were loaded.
This helped reduce technical overhead and create a more efficient
Shopify theme performance
setup.
Image optimization was also part of the process, ensuring that visual content could retain its role in the redesigned storefront without creating unnecessary loading costs.
The result was a more performance-conscious Shopify implementation built around both visual quality and technical efficiency.
Post-Migration SEO and Technical QA
The migration did not end when the new Shopify storefront went live.
A dedicated post-migration QA process was used to validate the new website across its main technical, ecommerce, and SEO layers.
We checked:
key website pages;
links and redirects;
responsive behavior across devices;
product catalog functionality;
shopping cart functionality;
Shopify Checkout;
technical SEO elements;
indexing and page accessibility.
This final validation was important because migration issues can appear only after the new platform is fully assembled.
By testing the storefront after implementation, we were able to verify that the new ecommerce system, SEO structure, and redesigned interface were working together as intended.
Combining Shopify Migration, SEO, and Performance
What makes the Parfums de Marly project particularly valuable is the combination of several complex objectives within one migration.
The project was not approached as:
WordPress → Shopify
Instead, it was treated as:
WordPress → Shopify + ecommerce transformation + redesign + SEO migration + performance optimization
Each part of the project influenced the others.

The ecommerce structure affected the information architecture. The redesign affected how content and products were presented. The new URL structure required redirects. SEO required careful content preservation and internal linking. Performance optimization had to account for the new Shopify theme and ecommerce functionality.
This integrated approach allowed the migration to improve the website on multiple levels simultaneously.
The Result: A Faster, SEO-Ready Shopify Ecommerce Foundation
Parfums de Marly was successfully migrated from WordPress to Shopify with a complete ecommerce structure, redesigned interface, SEO optimization, and performance improvements.
The new website provides users with a complete commercial journey:
discover product information;
explore the product catalog;
select products;
add products to the cart;
complete purchases through
Shopify Checkout
At the same time, the project preserved important content and SEO pages, introduced a more structured SEO foundation, improved internal linking, and addressed key technical performance factors.
The final result is a more modern and commercially capable
Shopify ecommerce website
with:
WordPress to Shopify migration
Shopify ecommerce development
Shopify custom storefront development
Shopify SEO migration
Shopify redirects and URL preservation
Shopify internal linking optimization
Shopify theme performance optimization
image and third-party script optimization
Core Web Vitals optimization
post-migration technical QA
For Crocode, Parfums de Marly is a strong example of
Shopify migration combined with SEO and performance optimization
— demonstrating how a platform change can become an opportunity to improve the entire ecommerce infrastructure rather than simply reproduce an existing website on a new CMS.

children.text: Brand Spirit and Project Scope

Laidback London produces footwear through traditional techniques in fair-trade workshops. Their customers value craftsmanship, sustainability, and effortless style. The brand personality feels approachable yet refined — casual but not careless.

The existing website failed to communicate these qualities. Generic templates made the brand indistinguishable from mass-market competitors. Product information lacked the depth conscious consumers expect. Mobile experience particularly disappointed given the target demographic.
Design Language Development

We developed a visual language reflecting handmade warmth. Textures suggest natural materials throughout the interface. Color palettes draw from leather, earth, and Mediterranean skies. Typography feels relaxed without losing professionalism.

The homepage invites exploration rather than pushing sales. Lifestyle photography shows products in authentic contexts. Brand story elements weave naturally through commercial content. The atmosphere welcomes visitors into the Laidback London world.
Product presentation emphasizes tactile qualities:
close-up photography reveals leather grain and stitching detail;
multiple angle views show construction quality;
lifestyle images demonstrate comfortable fit;
craft process documentation builds appreciation;
artisan stories connect buyers with actual makers.
These elements justify premium pricing while creating emotional connection.
Sustainability Communication

Conscious consumers research brand practices carefully before purchasing. We created a transparency framework sharing sustainability information clearly. Material sourcing details appear at product level. Workshop conditions document openly.

The impact dashboard quantifies environmental commitments. Customers see carbon offset tracking and waste reduction metrics. This transparency differentiates Laidback London from brands making vague claims.
Packaging information addresses common concerns. Recyclable materials, minimal plastic, and reusable elements appear prominently. Shipping impact calculations let customers understand their choices.
Size and Fit Solutions
Footwear returns often result from incorrect sizing. We attacked this problem through multiple approaches:
Detailed measurement guides.
Instructions cover foot length, width, and arch characteristics.
Brand comparison tools.
Customers relate sizes to familiar brands they already own.
Fit finder quiz.
Questions about foot shape and wearing habits generate personalized recommendations.
Model-specific notes.
Certain styles run differently and display warnings accordingly.
Customer fit feedback.
Reviews prominently feature sizing comments from actual buyers.
This community knowledge reduces sizing guesswork significantly. Returns dropped noticeably after implementation.
Technical Implementation Details

We optimized the store specifically for mobile shoppers who browse during commutes and coffee breaks. Touch targets sized appropriately for easy navigation. Image galleries swipe smoothly. Checkout flows minimized typing requirements.
The search function understands natural language queries. Customers find products by describing what they want. Results adapt to seasonal availability automatically.

Inventory connects with manufacturing planning. Lead times for made-to-order items display accurately. Customers understand when to expect handcrafted pieces requiring production time. Laidback London expanded their product range following platform launch — new categories including bags and accessories integrated smoothly.

children.text: Meeting the Needs of Outdoor Enthusiasts

Outdoor gear shoppers research exhaustively before spending. They compare weight measurements down to grams. They read waterproof ratings and temperature ranges carefully. Generic product descriptions fail these customers completely — they'll just go somewhere else.

Arcus came to us frustrated with their existing platform. Product data spread across inconsistent formats. Filtering options missed critical attributes like pack volume and insulation type. The search function returned irrelevant results too often.
Structured Product Information Architecture

We rebuilt the entire product data model from scratch. Every category received custom attribute sets matching how customers actually shop. Tents display capacity, seasonality, and packed dimensions prominently. Sleeping bags show temperature ratings and fill power clearly. No guessing required.

The comparison tool lets shoppers evaluate multiple products side by side. Specifications align in rows for easy scanning. Differences highlight automatically. This feature reduced return rates — customers choose correctly the first time when they have proper information.
Our information architecture included these specialized components:
gear compatibility matrices showing what works together;
weight calculators for building complete kit lists;
size guides with measurement instructions for apparel;
care instructions accessible from every product page;
warranty information displayed with claim procedures.
These tools transform shopping from guesswork into informed decision-making. Customers trust Arcus because they receive complete information upfront.
Visual Treatment for Adventure Products

Outdoor gear photography needs to convey durability and performance. We established photo standards showing products in actual use conditions. Tents appear pitched in varied terrain. Backpacks display properly loaded and worn. Customers see what they're actually buying.

Homepage features rotating adventure imagery that inspires purchase motivation. Video content shows gear tested in demanding environments. User-submitted photos create community connection and social proof.

Color choices throughout reflect natural environments. Earth tones dominate the palette. Accent colors come from technical fabrics in the product line. Typography feels sturdy without being heavy. The overall effect suggests capability and reliability.
Technical Performance Optimization

Outdoor enthusiasts often shop from areas with poor connectivity — planning next weekend's trip from a cabin, maybe. We optimized aggressively for slow network conditions. Images compress intelligently based on connection speed. Critical content loads first while secondary elements follow.
The optimization work addressed specific performance challenges:
Progressive image loading.
Thumbnails appear immediately with full resolution loading in background.
Content prioritization.
Essential product specs render before supplementary materials.
Offline capability.
Previously viewed products remain accessible when signal drops.
Connection detection.
System adjusts asset quality based on current bandwidth.
Aggressive caching.
Repeat visits load nearly instantly from local storage.
Page speed scores consistently reach 90 or above on mobile. This performance advantage helps search rankings and reduces bounce rates.
Integration with Expedition Planning

Arcus serves both casual hikers and serious expeditions. We built a trip planning module that helps customers prepare properly. They enter destination, duration, and activity type. The system generates gear checklists they can shop directly.

Group ordering functionality supports organized trips. Leaders create shared carts that team members contribute to. Bulk discounts apply automatically at quantity thresholds. Shipping consolidates to single addresses for departure points.

This planning integration drives significant order value increases. Customers who use the trip planner spend three times more than average. They return frequently as new adventures require additional equipment. Arcus expanded internationally following the Shopify migration — multi-language support and localized shipping options reduced cart abandonment from overseas visitors.
